newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end lower on March crude expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end lower on March crude expiry.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices were swept to a sharply lower finish Thursday by expiry-related selling in the March crude contract exacerbated by growing crude supply.

"The expiry played a part, but not exclusively," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney. "The crude build was big," said Saucer, referring to weekly oil inventory data released by the American Petroleum Institute (API) on Wednesday which showed a 3.1 million barrel build in crude stocks.
March crude settled 81 cents off at $21.98 a barrel.
Traders rolled positions out of the March contract into the April month ahead of March's expiry at session's end.

"Gasoline was weaker than heating oil - which has been the dog of the complex - after the gasoline spreads had blown out too early. There was plenty of weakness to go around," Saucer said of Thursday's price action.
March heating oil finished 1.55 cents lower at 58.04 cents a gallon, and March gasoline ended 1.90 cents off at 62.78 cents a gallon.
Traders said the gasoline-to-heating oil spread (in favor of gasoline) had widened sharply when the start of the anticipated spring gasoline rally was still a month a away.

Gasoline typically rallys in the spring ahead of the summer driving season when gasoline demand traditionally peaks. The gasoline-to-heat spread narrowed to 4.74 cents, consolidating gains after rising to 5.09 cents Wednesday from 3.44 cents last Friday.

Although the crude inventory build in the API report was in line with trader expectations, stock data for the same week ended February 14 from the Department of Energy's (DOE) Energy Information Administration (EIA) said crude stocks grew a larger 4.4 million barrels.

Moreover, the API data also showed a year-over-year crude surplus of 5.8 milllion barrels, the first year-over-year stock surplus since the week ended November 1, 1996 when there was a 3.1 million barrel surplus.
Adding to crude's bearish supply news, the United Nations sanctions committee on Iraq approved deeper discounts for Iraqi crude sales to the U.S., diplomatic sources said Thursday.
The committee allowed a special discount price of $4.30 below WTI for February and up to March 9, down from the originally agreed $3.85 under.
Oil traders said the increased discount for Iraqi barrels for the February/early March period might encourage even more Iraqi crude to head to the U.S. market.
Under a deal approved last December, the United Nations eased sanctions against Iraq and allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil for six months in exchange for humanitarian aid.
Chartists said April crude assumed its spot month role technically vulnerable, finishing a penny above its session low of $21.65.

April crude failed at trendline resistance of $22.30 extending from April's session high January 30 of $24.44 and closed below Wednesday's session low of $22.00, confirming a minor downside reversal, said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
